page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top, page number at top left. Below the running text: a verse continuation in italic (full width), a rule, a centred title with a subtitle, then a verse epitaph in italic with a large initial H. Catchword at bottom right.

p.i: Transtulit inferni cuncta in se mœnia regni, Imperio Pluto, fœdis Harpyia rapinis, Eumenis igne, Charon naulo, triplicique corona Cerberus, immissi stupefactus lumine veri, Terrificoque tua deiectus fulmine lingua Transferet infernas in se post funera pœnas: Inter aquas sitiens, referens revolubile saxum, Vulturibus iecur exsefus[?], caua dolia lymphis Frustra implens, Ixionium distentus in orbem.

HIC Nicolaum ne Baconem conditum Existima illum, tam diu Britannici Regni secundum columen, exitium malis, Bonis asylum: cæca quem non extulit Ad hunc honorem sors: sed æquitas, fides, Doctrina, pietas, unica & prudentia. Neu morte raptum crede: qui unica breui Vita perennes emerit duas: agit Vitam secundam cælites inter animas, Fama implet orbem, vita quæ illi tertia est. Hac posita in ara corpus animi olim domus, Ara dicata sempiternæ memoriæ.

page.notes: Small red marks in the right margin beside "Fama" and "Ara" are stains or printer's marks, not text, and are not transcribed. Doubtful readings: "exsefus" in the verse above (the word is blurred; the [?] marks it). "cæca" is read from the print. The ne in "Nicolaum ne Baconem" is as printed. The catchword "IOAN-" is taken as printed at the foot right.
